successors.name: Greek Dark Ages
successors.text: the palatial state of Mycenae with Tiryns and Nauplion: 'two to three times the size of the other palatial states' (40 km disc, 5,027 km2)

ledger.x: c. 1550: Mycenae becomes a major power. 'Mycenae developed into a major power during LHI (c. 1550 - c. 1450 BC)'; the shaft graves show 'extensive Cretan influence (Minoan) in the region from c. 1600 BC'. The land (the Argive plain) is the researcher's reading.

c. 1350: the palatial state at its peak includes the adjacent centres. 'Its territory would have also included adjacent centers, including Tiryns and Nauplion'; the page gives no date for their incorporation.

c. 1150: Mycenae destroyed. 'Mycenae was among the numerous Aegean sites destroyed as part of the Bronze Age Collapse around 1200 BC' and the collapse 'culminated in the destruction of Mycenae itself c. 1150 BC'; the causes are 'unknown' (enemy attack, internal strife, earthquakes). The page gives both 1200 and 1150.

certainty.note: No boundary is known; the territory is a disc of the size the page implies.
